pll1d46c1-d1e3509.summary: Raises the question: God's will, his good pleasure, cannot be frustrated, since he did all he willed and nothing resists him. How then is 1 Tim 2:4 ('wills all men to be saved') to be understood, since not all are saved? And Matt 23:37 ('how often I willed to gather your children, and you would not') suggests God's will was overcome by human will. Where then is his omnipotence?

pl-l1d46c1.summary: Raises the problem that God's will, his good pleasure, cannot be frustrated ('he did all he willed,' Ps 113:11; 'who resists his will?' Rom 9:19), yet Paul says God 'wills all men to be saved' (1 Tim 2:4) though many are damned, and Christ says 'how often I willed to gather your children, and you would not' (Matt 23:37), as if human will overcame God's.
